answer: Require each new agent to complete a verifiable public-good task, such as curating a small dataset, before its identity activates at a network vertex. A random audit panel rechecks a sample of the work, and only audited identities join the lotus registry that grants transaction rights. Creating many fake identities therefore costs skilled labor for each one, not just a copied script, while an opal audit trail lets peers re-verify disputed work. The limit is audit capacity: if submissions flood in, honest newcomers wait, so task difficulty and audit sampling must scale together.
